title: Topological spectral gap, multiscale Weyl's law, and homogenization in high-contrast PDEs
summary: This paper introduces a unified abstract variational and topological framework to characterize the spectral gap and eigenvalue distribution in high-contrast multiscale partial differential equations (PDEs). We rigorously prove that the exact location of the spectral gap is universally determined by the dimension of the local null space associated with the high-contrast inclusions. For systems with infinite-dimensional kernels, this location is strictly determined by the topological Betti numbers.
